toc.title: A first workflow and how to read a run
Jobs in parallel, in order, and as checks

html:
1The Actions model

GitHub Actions is the automation built into GitHub. Something happens in the repository, GitHub starts a workflow, and a fresh machine runs its steps. The figure shows how the parts nest.

Term What it is
Event Something that starts a workflow: a push, a pull request, a schedule, a click
Workflow One YAML file: which events start it and which jobs it runs
Job A set of steps on one runner; jobs run in parallel unless one needs another
Step One shell command (run) or one action (uses); steps run in order
Action A reusable unit of work, for example actions/checkout
Runner The server that runs one job; every job gets a fresh virtual machine

Workflows live in the folder .github/workflows as .yml or .yaml files. They are ordinary files: versioned, reviewed in pull requests and tied to a branch. A workflow runs on an event, on a schedule or by hand.

GitHub-hosted runners have labels such as ubuntu-latest (Ubuntu 24.04), windows-latest and macos-latest (on arm64). The -latest labels point to the newest stable image and can change. Standard runners are free in public repositories; private repositories use the compute included in the plan. Larger and self-hosted runners also exist (module 15).

Tip

. Treat workflow files as code: change them through a branch and a pull request. They sit in the repository like any other file, and a bad edit can break every later run or leak a secret.

2A first workflow and how to read a run

The smallest useful workflow runs on a push and by hand, prints a message and checks out the code. A runner starts empty, so a job that needs your files must run actions/checkout first.

# .github/workflows/hello.yml
name: Hello
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
jobs:
  hello:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - run: echo "Hello from shopfront"; ls
Key Meaning
on The events that start the workflow: a push to main, or a click on Run workflow
workflow_dispatch Lets someone start the run by hand; the file must be on the default branch for the Run workflow button
runs-on The runner label for the job
uses Runs an action; actions/checkout@v6 copies the repository onto the runner
run Runs shell commands; the default shell on Linux and macOS is bash -e {0}, so a step stops at its first failing command

Try it: save the file, commit it and push. Your hash will differ.

mkdir -p .github/workflows
# save the workflow above as .github/workflows/hello.yml
git add .github/workflows/hello.yml
git commit -m "Add hello workflow"
git push

[main 856a46f] Add hello workflow
 1 file changed, 12 insertions(+)
 create mode 100644 .github/workflows/hello.yml

After the push the run starts by itself. Open the Actions tab, choose the run, then choose a job to see its steps. Every step has its own log.

A failed step turns the job red, and the later steps are skipped unless their if: says otherwise. A run on a pull request also shows in the Checks tab of that PR.

Tip

. Start every job that needs your code with actions/checkout. Each job gets a fresh runner, and a fresh runner has no copy of the repository.

3Triggers and filters

The on key chooses the events. Filters narrow an event so the workflow does not run for every change.

Event Starts when Details
push Commits are pushed Filters: branches, branches-ignore, tags, tags-ignore, paths, paths-ignore
pull_request A PR is opened, gets new commits or is reopened These are the default types; no run while the PR has a merge conflict
workflow_dispatch Someone clicks Run workflow inputs of type string, number, boolean, choice or environment
schedule A cron time arrives POSIX cron in UTC, never more often than every 5 minutes; runs on the default branch

A cron line has five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. In a public repository a scheduled workflow is disabled automatically after 60 days without activity.

# .github/workflows/triggers.yml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ["src/**"]
  pull_request:
  schedule:
    - cron: "30 5 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs: {target: {type: choice, options: [staging, production]}}
jobs:
  t: {runs-on: ubuntu-latest, steps: [{run: echo triggered}]}

This file starts on a push to main that changes a file under src, on every pull request, every Monday at 05:30 UTC and on a click that offers staging or production.

Tip

. If a required check comes from a workflow with a path filter, remember that a skipped workflow leaves the check Pending. The pull request then waits for a result that never comes.

4Contexts, variables and conditions

The text ${{ ... }} is an expression. GitHub replaces it with its value before the step runs. The values come from contexts.

Context Example What it holds
github ${{ github.ref }} Facts about the run, such as the branch or tag (refs/heads/main) and github.event_name
env ${{ env.APP }} Variables set with env:; a step beats a job, and a job beats the workflow
vars ${{ vars.REGION }} Plain, non-secret variables saved in the repository settings
secrets ${{ secrets.TOKEN }} Secret values saved in Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions; an unset secret is an empty string

An if: condition decides whether a job or step runs. Write it without the braces: if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'. After a failure, if: always() still runs a step and if: failure() runs it only when an earlier step failed. A secret cannot be used directly in an if:; module 14 shows the way around it.

Tip

. Hand ${{ }} values to a step through env: and read them as shell variables. The script then holds a plain $REF instead of text pasted in by GitHub, which is safer for values that people can write (module 15).

5Jobs in parallel, in order, and as checks

Jobs run in parallel by default, each on its own runner. They share nothing unless you upload and download an artifact (module 14). The key needs makes a job wait for one or more others, and it does not start if a job it needs failed.

# .github/workflows/jobs.yml
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  lint: {runs-on: ubuntu-latest, steps: [{run: echo lint}]}
  test: {runs-on: ubuntu-latest, steps: [{run: echo test}]}
  report:
    needs: [lint, test]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env: {REF: "${{ github.ref }}"}
    steps:
      - run: echo "report for $REF"

Here lint and test start together. report waits for both and runs only on the main branch.

A workflow with the pull_request trigger runs on the pull request. Each of its jobs shows as a check in the Checks tab and in the merge box. An admin can make a check required in a branch protection rule or a ruleset (module 11), and then the pull request cannot merge until that check is green.

6Practice Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A workflow has on: workflow_dispatch, but the Run workflow button is missing. The file exists only on a feature branch. What fixes it?

  • AAdd the push event to the on block of the file
  • BMerge the workflow file into the default branch
  • CRename the file so that it ends with .yaml instead
  • DMove the job into a separate reusable workflow
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Run workflow button needs the workflow file on the default branch.

S2A workflow uses cron: "0 6 * * 1", and the team works far from the UTC time zone. When does the schedule run?

  • AEvery Monday at 06:00 in the time zone of whoever saved the file
  • BEvery Monday at 06:00 in the time zone of the repository owner
  • CEvery Monday at 06:00 UTC, whatever the local time zone is
  • DEvery Monday at 06:00 on the clock of the runner's region
Show the answer

Answer: C. Scheduled workflows use POSIX cron in UTC by default.

S3A run page shows lint green, test red and report skipped. The report job has needs: [lint, test]. Why was it skipped?

  • AThe lint job finished before the test job started
  • BThe report job ran out of free runners in the plan
  • CJobs only run in the order in which they are written
  • DA job that it needs failed, so it never started
Show the answer

Answer: D. A job with needs does not start when one of the jobs it needs failed.

S4A step reads ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}, but nobody has created that secret yet. What does the step get?

  • AAn empty string, and the run keeps going
  • BThe literal text secrets.API_KEY in its place
  • CAn error that stops the run before it starts
  • DThe value of a variable called API_KEY
Show the answer

Answer: A. An unset secret is evaluated as an empty string.

S5A required check comes from a workflow with paths: ["src/**"]. A pull request changes only README.md. What does the pull request show?

  • AThe check turns green because nothing needed testing
  • BThe check stays Pending because the filter skipped it
  • CThe check turns red because no job returned a result
  • DThe workflow runs anyway because a PR ignores filters
Show the answer

Answer: B. A workflow skipped by a filter leaves its required check Pending.

S6A job has one step, run: ls, and the listing is empty although the repository has files. What is the likely cause?

  • AThe default shell hides files that start with a dot
  • BThe ls command is not installed on Linux runners
  • CThe job has no checkout step, so the runner has no code
  • DFiles appear only after the workflow has run once
Show the answer

Answer: C. Each job starts on a fresh runner, so it needs actions/checkout to get the code.

6.2 Recall questions

R1In which folder do workflow files live?

Show the answer

.github/workflows.

R2What is the difference between a job and a step?

Show the answer

A job is a set of steps on one runner; a step is one command or one action.

R3Which event adds a Run workflow button?

Show the answer

workflow_dispatch.

R4Which time zone does a schedule cron use?

Show the answer

UTC.

R5Which key makes one job wait for another?

Show the answer

needs.

R6Which context holds the plain variables saved in the repository settings?

Show the answer

vars.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Model event starts a workflow; a workflow has jobs; a job has steps and one runner; a step runs a command or an action
Where .github/workflows, .yml or .yaml, reviewed like code
First workflow on push and workflow_dispatch; runs-on; actions/checkout; run
Triggers push and pull_request with filters; schedule in UTC; workflow_dispatch needs the default branch
Contexts github, env, vars, secrets inside ${{ }}; hand values over with env:
Conditions if: without braces; always() and failure(); no secrets directly
Jobs parallel by default; needs makes order; a failed need skips the job
Checks pull_request jobs become checks; a skipped filter leaves a required check Pending
